reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, wide-packet re-review batch 3, 2026-08-01

samples_reviewed.question_text: A rectangle has sides 11 cm and 2 cm. What is its perimeter?
A rectangle has sides 1 cm and 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
A rectangle has sides 2 cm and 7 cm. What is its perimeter?
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: 4 of 7 samples (44, 45, 50, 68) are the generic single-object prompt 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.' or 'How long is the object?', which never mentions perimeter or a multi-sided figure at all.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The 3 on-topic samples (42, 43, 46) all compute perimeter arithmetically from two given side lengths, e.g. seed 42's 'A rectangle has sides 11 cm and 2 cm. What is its perimeter?'; none shows the student using a measuring tool on a drawn figure, the 'measure ... using appropriate tools' half of the competency.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Both the perimeter-arithmetic items and the length-reading items use short, direct sentences appropriate for Grade 2 Quarter 4.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The length-measurement samples (44, 45, 50, 68) are copied from the plain object-length-measuring competency rather than being genuine perimeter-tool variants of this node.

competency_alignment.rationale: Over half the sample pool (seeds 44, 45, 50, 68) builds single-object length-reading skill, an axis distinct from identifying/measuring the perimeter of a plane figure.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Where perimeter is actually tested, side lengths (1-11 cm, totals 12-26 cm at seeds 42, 43, 46) are a reasonable Grade 2 magnitude.
